Scan a Kubernetes cluster, YAML files, Helm charts, Kustomize directories, Git repositories, or container images for security misconfigurations and vulnerabilities.

Usage:
  kubescape scan [flags]
  kubescape scan [command]

Examples:

  Scan command is for scanning an existing cluster or kubernetes manifest files based on pre-defined frameworks

  # Scan current cluster
  kubescape scan

  # Scan kubernetes manifest files
  kubescape scan .

  # Scan and save the results in the JSON format
  kubescape scan --format json --output results.json

  # Scan and save the results in multiple format in a single scan
  kubescape scan --format json,html,junit --output result

  # Display all resources
  kubescape scan --verbose

  # Generate an anonymized report
  kubescape scan --hide --format json -o report.json

  # The key is a passphrase of at least 16 characters. It is stretched into an
  # AES-256 key with Argon2id under a per-report salt, so length is what buys
  # you security here — prefer a long passphrase or generated key material.
  export KUBESCAPE_MASTER_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
  # Hex-encoded key material works too, via a separate variable:
  # export KUBESCAPE_MASTER_KEY_HEX="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
  kubescape scan --encrypt --format json -o encrypted-report.json

  # Decrypt an encrypted report
  kubescape decrypt encrypted-report.json > decrypted-report.json

  # Scan different clusters from the kubectl context
  kubescape scan --kube-context <kubernetes context>

  # Compare a live scan against a saved baseline report and fail CI on new high-severity+ drift
  kubescape scan --baseline base.json --baseline-fail-on-new --baseline-severity-threshold high

help.text:
Kubescape is a tool for testing Kubernetes security posture. Docs: https://kubescape.io/docs/

Usage:
  kubescape [command]

Examples:

  # Scan a Kubernetes cluster or YAML files for image vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
  kubescape scan

  # List supported controls
  kubescape list controls

  # Download artifacts (air-gapped environment support)
  kubescape download artifacts

  # View cached configurations
  kubescape config view


Available Commands:
  completion    Generate autocompletion script
  config        Handle cached configurations
  decrypt       Decrypt a report produced by kubescape scan --encrypt
  diff          Compare two Kubescape scan JSON reports and show what changed
  download      Download artifacts,attack-tracks,control,controls-inputs,exceptions,framework
  fix           Propose a fix for the misconfiguration found when scanning Kubernetes manifest files
  help          Help about any command
  list          List frameworks/controls will list the supported frameworks and controls
  mcpserver     Start the Kubescape MCP server
  operator      The operator is used to communicate with the Kubescape Operator within the cluster components.
  patch         Patch container images to fix known OS-level vulnerabilities
  prerequisites Check prerequisites for installing Kubescape Operator
  scan          Scan a Kubernetes cluster or YAML files for image vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
  update        Update to latest release version
  vap           Helper commands for managing Validating Admission Policies in a Kubernetes cluster
  version       Get current version

fix.--no-confirm: No confirmation will be given to the user before applying the fix (default false)
fix.--skip-user-values: Changes which involve user-defined values will be skipped (default true)

mcpserver.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context

operator.--confirm: perform the real cluster write; without it the action is a dry-run preview
operator.--finding-ref: scan-result reference that justifies the action, e.g. workloadconfigurationscansummaries/payments/api
operator.--kind: target workload kind: Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet or Pod
operator.--reason: human-readable justification recorded in the audit trail

patch.--address: Address of buildkitd service, defaults to the local docker daemon with fallback to unix:///run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock
patch.--format: Output file format. Supported formats: pretty-printer, json, junit, prometheus, pdf, html, sarif, gitlab-sast, yaml, cyclonedx-json, spdx-json
patch.--ignore-errors: Ignore errors and continue patching other images. Default to false
patch.--image: Application image name and tag to patch
patch.--output: Output file. Print output to file and not stdout
patch.--output-mode: Output mode for the patched image (docker, image, oci, local) (default "docker")
patch.--output-path: Destination path for oci or local output mode
patch.--password: Password for registry login. Prefer the environment variable: a flag value is visible in ps and shell history [$KUBESCAPE_REGISTRY_PASSWORD]
patch.--push: Push the patched image to the source registry. Default to false (the patched image is only loaded into the local image store). If set, this overrides output-mode to 'image'.
patch.--severity-threshold: Severity threshold is the severity of a vulnerability at which the command fails and returns exit code 1
patch.--tag: Tag for the patched image. Defaults to '<image-tag>-patched'
patch.--timeout: Timeout for the operation, defaults to '5m' (default 5m0s)
patch.--use-default-matchers: Use default matchers (true) or CPE matchers (false) for image scanning (default true)
patch.--verbose: Display full report. Default to false
patch.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context

prerequisites.--kubeconfig: Path to the kubeconfig file. If not set, in-cluster config is used or $HOME/.kube/config if outside a cluster.
prerequisites.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context

scan.--access-key: Kubescape SaaS access key. Default will load access key from cache
scan.--account: Kubescape SaaS account ID. Default will load account ID from cache
scan.--audit-exceptions: Include an exception usage audit in supported scan outputs
scan.--baseline: Path to a saved JSON scan report to diff the fresh scan against.
scan.--baseline-fail-on-new: With --baseline, exit with code 1 when new failures are found versus the baseline.
scan.--baseline-granularity: With --baseline, comparison unit: evidence or control. (default "evidence")
scan.--baseline-severity-threshold: With --baseline, only count new failures at or above this severity when using --baseline-fail-on-new.
scan.--cluster-name: Set the custom name of the cluster. Not same as the kube-context flag
scan.--compliance-threshold: Compliance threshold is the percent below which the command fails and returns exit code 1. Applies to 'scan framework', 'scan control', and '--view resource|control'
scan.--control-timeout: Maximum duration for evaluating a single control (e.g. 30s, 1m). 0 means no timeout. Controls that exceed this are marked as not evaluated and the scan continues. Must be lower than --scan-timeout when both are set.
scan.--controls-config: Path to an controls-config obj. If not set will download controls-config from ARMO management portal
scan.--controls-version: Pin the regolibrary release tag used to download controls (see https://github.com/kubescape/regolibrary/releases). If not used will download the latest release. Has no effect when --account is set (cloud backend is used instead)
scan.--dry-run: Check whether the current credentials can list every resource type the requested policies need, without collecting resources or evaluating controls. Cluster scans only.
scan.--enable-rego-prints: Enable sending to rego prints to the logs (use with debug log level: -l debug)
scan.--enable-streaming: Enable resource streaming for large clusters to reduce memory usage. Resources are processed in batches instead of loading all at once. Automatically enabled for clusters with >2500 resources.
scan.--encrypt: Encrypt sensitive report metadata using the KUBESCAPE_MASTER_KEY environment variable
scan.--exceptions: Path to an exceptions obj. If not set will download exceptions from ARMO management portal
scan.--exclude-kinds: exclude the specified Kubernetes resource kinds from the scan (case-insensitive, Kind name only — not group/version qualified). e.g: --exclude-kinds Job,CronJob
scan.--exclude-namespaces: Namespaces to exclude from scanning. e.g: --exclude-namespaces ns-a,ns-b. Notice, when running with exclude-namespace kubescape does not scan cluster-scoped objects.
scan.--fail-coverage-below: Fail (exit code 1) when the scan coverage score drops below this percentage (0 to disable). The score is the ratio of evaluated controls discounted by 3 points per silent failed GVR pull (a resource type that failed to collect entirely but whose dependent controls still evaluated via other resource types), 2 points per partial GVR pull, and 5 points per degraded policy input, so a scan with every control evaluated can still fail on partial resource collection or fallback policy inputs
scan.--fail-on-degraded-config: Fail the scan (exit code 1) if control configurations or exceptions could not be loaded from their configured source and bundled defaults were used instead
scan.--hide: Replace sensitive report metadata with deterministic pseudonyms
scan.--honor-inline-exceptions: Honor kubescape.io/skip-* annotations as inline exception policies. By default this is enabled when scanning local manifest files and disabled for live-cluster scans
scan.--host-scan: Enable host data collection from cluster nodes for certain controls. When not set, Kubescape auto-detects node-agent CRDs and uses a CRD-based host sensor if available. Use --host-scan=false to disable host data collection. See https://github.com/kubescape/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/kubescape-operator for the operator-based alternative
scan.--image-platform: OCI platform for --scan-images, for example linux/amd64; overrides platform inferred from workload scheduling constraints
scan.--image-scan-concurrency: Number of concurrent workers for image scanning (default 1)
scan.--include-kinds: scan only the specified Kubernetes resource kinds (case-insensitive, Kind name only — not group/version qualified). e.g: --include-kinds Deployment,DaemonSet
scan.--keep-local: If you do not want your Kubescape results reported to configured backend.
scan.--kubeconfig: Paths to a kubeconfig. Only required if out-of-cluster.
scan.--label-selector: Filter collected Kubernetes resources by label selector. Accepts any selector that kubectl -l supports, e.g: --label-selector app=nginx,env!=dev
scan.--labels-to-copy: Labels to copy from workloads to scan reports for easy identification. e.g: --labels-to-copy=app,team,environment
scan.--max-severity: Only include controls at or below this severity (low, medium, high, critical) in the output
scan.--min-severity: Only include controls at or above this severity (low, medium, high, critical) in the output
scan.--only-fixable: When used with --severity-threshold on image scans, only count CVEs that have an available fix toward the pass/fail decision
scan.--output: Output file. Print output to file and not stdout
scan.--registry-authority: Registry host[:port] the --scan-images credentials apply to
scan.--registry-mapping: Map internal registry hosts to reachable ones, e.g. --registry-mapping image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000=registry.company.com (host[:port], no scheme) (default [])
scan.--registry-password: Password for image registry login when no docker config or credential helper is available; can also be set with KUBESCAPE_REGISTRY_PASSWORD
scan.--registry-token: Bearer token for image registry login when no docker config or credential helper is available; can also be set with KUBESCAPE_REGISTRY_TOKEN
scan.--registry-username: Username for image registry login when no docker config or credential helper is available; can also be set with KUBESCAPE_REGISTRY_USERNAME
scan.--release-name: Helm release name made available as .Release.Name when rendering the chart
scan.--release-namespace: Helm release namespace made available as .Release.Namespace when rendering the chart
scan.--scan-timeout: Maximum duration for the scan (e.g. 5m, 30s, 1h). 0 means no timeout. When the timeout is reached the scan exits with a non-zero code.
scan.--set: Set Helm values on the command line when scanning a Helm chart (can specify multiple, e.g. --set key1=val1 --set key2=val2)
scan.--set-file: Set Helm values from respective files specified via the command line (can specify multiple)
scan.--set-string: Set Helm STRING values on the command line when scanning a Helm chart (can specify multiple)
scan.--severity-threshold: Severity threshold is the severity of failed controls at which the command fails and returns exit code 1. Failed controls whose severity is unknown (missing base score) are treated as exceeding any threshold
scan.--show-evidence: Show evidence paths with current field values for each failed control (pretty-printer only)
scan.--show-secrets: Show secret field values in evidence output. By default secret values are redacted. Only effective with --show-evidence
scan.--skip-db-update: Do not update the vulnerability database before scanning images. Uses the locally cached database; fails if none is cached.
scan.--submit: Submit the scan results to Kubescape SaaS where you can see the results in a user-friendly UI, choose your preferred compliance framework, check risk results history and trends, manage exceptions, get remediation recommendations and much more. By default the results are not submitted
scan.--use-artifacts-from: Load artifacts from local directory. If not used will download them
scan.--use-default: Load local policy object from default path. If not used will download latest
scan.--use-default-matchers: Use default matchers (true) or CPE matchers (false) for image scanning (default true)
scan.--use-from: Load local policy object from specified path. If not used will download latest
scan.--values: Specify Helm values in a YAML file or a URL when scanning a Helm chart (can specify multiple, or separate paths with commas)
scan.--verbose: Display all of the input resources and not only failed resources
scan.--view: View results based on the resource/control/security. default is --view=security (default "security")
scan.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context
scan.--platform: OCI platform to scan, for example linux/amd64 or linux/arm64/v8
scan.--api-version: API version of the workload (e.g. apps/v1). Default will be empty.
scan.--chart-path: Path to the helm chart the workload is part of. Must be used with --file-path.
scan.--namespace: Namespace of the workload. Default will be empty.

update.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context

vap.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context
vap.--action: Action to take when policy fails, repeatable (Deny, Warn, Audit). Deny and Warn cannot be combined (default [Deny])
vap.--control: Kubescape control ID to bind resources to
vap.--output: Write output to file instead of stdout
vap.--policy: Name of the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to bind resources to
vap.--resource-rule: Restrict the binding to a group/version/resource the policy already matches, repeatable (e.g. apps/v1/deployments, /v1/pods). Omit to bind everything the policy matches
vap.--from-release: Download the library from this cel-admission-library release tag (e.g. v0.11) instead of using the embedded copy
vap.--timeout: HTTP request timeout per download, only used with --from-release (e.g. 30s, 1m). 0 disables the timeout (default 30s)

version.--kube-context: Kube context. Default will use the current-context
